opening_message:
Ticket 1: Maurice Perez (employee ID E036) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. Write is within the allowed maximum for full-time employees, so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Maurice Perez (E036) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors with basic training may have at most read access to Source Code. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: The requested access is write to Source Code. Evidence conflicts on employment type: HR lists full_time (max write, admin only if role owns the system), while Security's looked-up database lists contractor with basic security training, whose maximum for Source Code is read (contractors never admin; write requires advanced training). Given the Security database explicitly identifies the employee as a contractor with basic training, the applicable maximum is read. Since write exceeds this maximum, grant read.
